newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wrightson full yr forecast revised down.
newsitem.headline: Wrightson full yr forecast revised down.

text.p: New Zealand rural service company Wrightson Ltd on Thursday sharply lowered its full year forecast to NZ$12-16 million from an adjusted $20-23 million forecast.
It earlier announced a half year profit of $1.25 million for the six months to December 31 against the previous $5.74 million.

"Trading conditions are expected to remain difficult for some time yet, but Wrightson is on track with a strategic redirection of its business which we are confident will restore growth in earnings and shareholder value over the medium and
longer terms," Chairman Sir Ronald Trotter said.

The previous full year forecast was for a $24-27 million profit which did not include one-off factors. The new forecast includes a $2.2 million loss associated with the sale of Wrightson Bloodstock and second half earnings foregone, as well as Wrightson's restructuring programme.
The lower forecast is due mainly to a deterioration in trading conditions not anticipated when the previous forecast was announced.

Wrightson announced a reduced dividend of 2.5 cent from 3.5 cents which reflected reduced trading and cash flow performance. Net operating cash flow for the half year saw a deficit of $26.7 million against a deficit of $8.9 million for the year ago period. First half cash flow deficits are expected and the position was expected to improve significantly in the second half.
The deterioration is due to restructuring costs, the deterioration in the trading position and an increase in net debtors.
As well, some cost reduction benefits from restructuring had not been achieved as rapidly as planned.
The trading results for January 1997 were in line with the revised profit forecast range.
In the half year, Wrightson Farmers Finance Ltd achieved a net profit after tax of $4.5 million while Wrightson's General Activities made a loss after tax of $3.25 million.
The loss in general activities included a number of adverse non-recurring items including:
* a $854,000 loss from the sale of Wrightson Bloodstock
* Costs of $1.4 million associated with restructuring costs outside a restructuring provision established in 1995/96.
Wrightson said because of restructuring its results for the half were not truly comparable with the previous results.

In the half year, the finance, insurance broking, wool, retail, nutrition and farm consultancy businesses all made profits but the real estate and livestock businesses made losses before interest and tax.
Wrightson said it had made sound progress with its restructuring. It had 1,518 employees at December 31 against 1,670 at June 30, 1996. It plans further staff cuts during the next 12 months.
In 1995/96 it made a $17.5 million restructuring provision and by December 31 it had incurred costs of $4.7 million relating to that. Most costs came from redundancies.
Wrightson said it was confident the provision was adequate.
